newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah softens, band rumours diminish.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah softens, band rumours diminish.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah softened against the dollar in early trading on Tuesday, dealers said.
One local bank dealer said Singapore operators were seen buying dollars after the economic deregulation package did not contain a widening of the central bank intervention band.
"There is no fresh factor to trade on. The package contains nothing about the band," the dealer said, adding that players were covering part of their short dollar positions.
Spot rupiah was at 2,433.0/33.5 at 0225 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,431.00/31.75. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,432.75/33.10 and 2,432.25/32.75, respectively.
Indonesia unveiled an economic deregulation package which cut tariffs on 1,600 items. The government also moved to limit loans to the property sector to anticipate undesirable effects.
However, the central bank did not announce anything linked to the widely-speculated widening of the dollar-rupiah band, removing some of the arguments for going short in dollars.
But some analysts said sentiment remained positive because the package could stimulate the stock market which has posted several record highs in the past few days.
One Japanese bank dealer said the rupiah could benefit from the package on the back of increased investments.
A dealer in Singapore said overall trading was quiet, with a biddish tone on the dollar against the baht seen causing a slight weakening of the rupiah.
"It's a quiet day. In the swap market rates are trapped in a narrow range because of a two-way market," he said.
Liqudity was sufficient, with overnight rates trading at around 13.0/14.0 percent. Overnight swaps were at 0.3/0.4 and tom/next at 0.38/0.42 points.
One-month swaps were at 14.00/14.25, two at 26.5/27.5, three at 40.0/41.0 and six at 81.5/83.5 points.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,428/2,620 and the conversion band also by one point to 2,428/2,476 on Monday.
